subject: Close date variance: cordon, ownership, and MAP adjustments
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme — observed close variance & immediate asks

Team,

Quick summary from last night's sync with Acme: their evaluation gating (security review + performance benchmark) is slipping by ~2 weeks due to an internal procurement hold on the FIPS module and a throughput spike in our benchmark that we need to investigate. They flagged the close date (contractually targeted for 2026-07-09) as at-risk.

Immediate asks:
- Aditya: produce a compact MAP that isolates the gating items (security evidence, performance patch, go/no-go decision) with owners and hard dates. Aim for a MAP v3 that compresses the critical path where possible.
- Laura: liaison with procurement contact at Acme and confirm whether the hold is legal/PO related or purely compliance docs. If PO timing is uncertain, we need procurement milestone in MAP.
- Rishi: quick triage of the throughput regression (seen against the 16k token stress test). If a kernel fallback is acceptable for the short term, list the perf delta and rollback plan.

I attached the baseline MAP we used (MAP_Acme_v2.xlsx) and my notes. We should aim to get an updated MAP and a short risk log by EOD tomorrow so we can share with Olivia and bring her confidence back.

This thread should remain internal until we have an agreed next-step package.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_Acme_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close date variance: cordon, ownership, and MAP adjustments

Vivek — thanks for the heads up.

To be transparent, procurement has paused on the PO until we validate the FIPS path; security also slowed our internal bench because they want to see the end-to-end KMS flow (we asked for a diagram and test matrix). From our side the business stake is high — we were planning a phased go-live aligned to our Q3 campaign. Sliding past 7/9 puts that at risk.

Requests from Acme side:
- We need a one-page MAP we can circulate to our CIO and procurement with concrete owners and dates (no more than 3 high-risk items).
- If you anticipate more than a week of drift, please include a mitigation that preserves a limited-scope early delivery for the marketing integration.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call this afternoon if that helps.

—Olivia
Olivia Barnes
Director, Product Operations | Acme Corp
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@acme.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close date variance: cordon, ownership, and MAP adjustments

Olivia — thanks for the clarity and for looping procurement. Forwarding our proposed short package below and attaching MAP_Acme_v3.xlsx and the SOW redlines (SOW_Acme_redlines.pdf).

Executive summary (proposed rebaseline):
- New target close: 2026-07-23 (two-week slip + 2-day buffer).
- Early-scope delivery (marketing integration): targeted feature subset to be delivered by 2026-07-09 if the procurement hold is cleared for a limited scope PO.

Top 3 MAP milestones (owners | date):
1) Security evidence pack (Laura) — deliver diagrams & KMS test matrix by 2026-06-18.
2) Kernel/perf mitigation (Rishi) — implement temporary kernel fallback and run benchmark by 2026-06-22 (perf delta ~8-12% estimated).
3) Procurement milestone (Acme / Laura) — provisional PO for early-scope by 2026-06-25.

Risk log (high level):
- Procurement hold -> mitigation: provisional early-scope PO; Redwood will accept phased SOW.
- Perf regression on long-sequence tests -> mitigation: kernel fallback + targeted quantization profile; regression risk tracked.
- Security evidence gap -> mitigation: dedicated evidence pack + optional live walkthrough with security team.

Compensating offer: if final close slips beyond 2026-07-23 due to delivery issues on the Redwood side, we propose a one-time service credit up to 10% of first-year commitment (to be finalized by legal). This is conditional on the MAP and the SOW redlines we attached (so we can lock in scope).

Next steps:
- Olivia: confirm whether Acme can accept the proposed new close (2026-07-23) and whether the provisional PO for early scope is feasible.
- Laura/Rishi: confirm internal commitment to the dates above; if not possible, call out blockers by EOD today.

Thanks — I’ll hold a 20-minute readout if Olivia says yes to a call.

--
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_Acme_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet); SOW_Acme_redlines.pdf (PDF)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: approval request for short-term burst and credit policy (Acme MAP)

Laura / Rishi —

Following Aditya's proposed MAP v3 and the ask from Acme, I need two quick decisions from leadership to keep the rebaseline credible for the customer:

1) Approve a short-term engineering burst: +2 SWE-equivalents for 4 weeks (July 6–July 31) to own the kernel fallback and the early-scope delivery work. Estimated incremental cost is ~$48k. This is refundable via the proposed service credit structure if delivery misses the new close date.

2) Approve the one-time customer credit guardrail: up to 10% of first-year commitment as a cap on the credit we can offer if the delay is on Redwood. Legal will draft the exact language, but we need to signal this as a firm cap to Acme.

Rationale: without these two levers the MAP will look optimistic to the customer and procurement will push closure out further. The proposed credit is intentionally limited — it protects both parties and gives Acme commercial comfort.

Please reply with APPROVE / DECLINE / NEEDS INFO by EOD tomorrow so we can finalize the MAP and send to Olivia.

Attached: short risk log excerpt and MAP_Acme_v3.xlsx.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_Acme_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)
